premises.text: Video post-production feedback is slowed by email threads, meetings, calls, and spreadsheets instead of focused collaboration on the cut
premises.evidence_span: one minute of the final product takes up to 17 hours of post-production. Well, part of the problem is a lot of teams are running around, sifting through emails with long threads

premises.text: First Cut Pro viewing rooms collect timestamped video feedback with auto-pause, threaded replies, and quick-comment hotkeys
premises.evidence_span: all Paul needs to do is drop in a link, and he creates a viewing room

premises.text: Feedback digests can be assigned to editors and exported as markers into editing software such as Adobe Premiere
premises.evidence_span: we've also made it very easy for Tony to then export it directly into his favorite video editing software

premises.text: Browser-based product uses existing hosting infrastructure so IT has little to deploy, aiding adoption across team sizes and content types
premises.evidence_span: IT departments specifically love us because it's browser-based, and we leverage existing hosting infrastructure

premises.text: Project-based pricing is friendly to small teams while capturing upside from larger clients, with Adobe native integration and MPAA guideline compliance underway
premises.evidence_span: we're introducing project based pricing that's friendly to teams of all sizes

value.text: Video teams collaborate and manage post-production feedback efficiently on the cut itself
value.evidence_span: First Cut Pro is a communication and project management tool for video professionals

causal_links.evidence_span: Instead of doing emails and back and forth, all Paul needs to do is drop in a link
we've made it very, very easy to collect timestamp feedback
Basically, they really don't have to do anything
We want to make it affordable for small teams while keep on producing upsides for larger clients

notes: Email/calendar/call/spreadsheet frictions folded as one post-production communication problem (§4.1.6). Viewing-room feedback UX cascade folded; assignment+NLE export kept as actionable package of that review tool (§4.1.7). Intra-firm growth numbers treated as traction/network-effect evidence. Pricing + Adobe + MPAA announcements grouped as commercial/institutional packaging of the offering. Four-domain partition; not a need/product/money triad.
